newsitem.title: TAIWAN: TAIWAN CENTRAL BANK INJECTS T$6 BLN IN FUND.
newsitem.headline: TAIWAN CENTRAL BANK INJECTS T$6 BLN IN FUND.

text.p: Taiwan's central bank, responding to rising money rates on tight liquidity, injected T$6 billion worth of funds into the banking system through open market operations on Friday afternoon, a central bank official said.
The bank had launched a T$9 billion injection on Friday morning.
For the afternoon injection, the bank executed a repurchase of negotiable certificates of deposit offered by interested financial institutions with a rate of 8.50 percent.
The institutions have the option of repurchasing the NCDs between eight and 10 years, the official said.
The overnight interbank rate finished at 8.862 percent on Thursday against Wednesday's 8.748 percent close, well above the central bank's 5.0-5.5 percent target zone.
The rate stood at 9.216 percent at 0745 GMT on Friday.
